_doc: Batch m08 (medium, opus themed pass): beaded lizard, monitors (tree, water, spice, komodo pup) and snakes (smooth, water, tree, night adder, sidewinder, dune racer). Motifs in motifs/medium_m08.js; every creature has its own signature motif, shared reptile motifs: fork-tongue, venom-fang, scale-shingle, venom-spit (+ m06 fish-toss).

beaded-lizard.notes: A heavy, slow beaded lizard (Gila kin) of desert and dry forest, its hide rows of orange and black beads; it does not strike, it bites, clamps on and chews its venom in.

p.u0: Bead Flash: the orange-and-black bead hide flips colours in a warning flash, beads scattering out and snapping back

u1.n: Dodge Roll: the heavy beaded lizard lumbers aside off the edge and plods back, desert dust kicked up

p.u2: Venom Chew: blunt beaded jaws clamp and chew, venom welling along the jaw grooves and dripping off the edge

u3.n: Won't Let Go: the jaws lock out on the edge and stay clamped, chewing, angry marks popping

b0.n: Slow Gnaw Hold: the beaded head shoves out, gnaws and drags back slowly

b1.n: Bead Tail Thrash: fat banded tails thrash out of the edge like clubs

b2.n: Beaded Hide: bead-scales line the edge in a tight armoured mosaic, a slow orange-black ripple through them

b3.n: Oozing Chew: chewing jaws let venom ooze and splat into a dark pool below

tree-monitor.notes: A slim green tree monitor of forest and island canopies that lies flat along a branch with its long tail curled round it, then drops onto prey from above.

u0.n: Branch Lash: long banded tails whip out between spots and crack, tied in a tripping line

p.u1: Bark Blend: bark patches line the edge, a lizard eye opens in the bark, glances, and is gone

u2.n: Venom Drip: green venom beads swell on leaf tips and drop on their threads

u3.n: Monitor Canopy Drop: the monitor lets go of its branch, slams out of the edge and drops back

p.b0: Branch Drop Bite: monitors on their branches lunge off the edge and bite

b1.n: Canopy Coil Whip: one long tail uncoils and cracks along the whole edge

b2.n: Bough-Ridged Scales: green keeled scales shingle along the edge like bark ridges

b3.n: Overhead Venom Dribble: leaf tips drip venom beads from overhead, dew running

water-monitor.notes: A long dark water monitor of wetland and coast that swims with its tail sculling side to side and wallows in mud with only its eyes showing.

u0.n: Tail Sweep: a heavy tail winds up and hammers out of the edge, water bursting in a splash fan

p.u1: Wallow Plate: mud slabs line the edge, the monitor's eyes and nostrils just above, ripples widening

u2.n: Waterline Shove: the swimming monitor shoves out along the waterline and slides back, bubbles rising

u3.n: Silt Dive: the monitor dives, silt clouds bloom out and settle, a tail tip vanishing

p.b0: River Lizard Bite: swimming monitors launch off the edge, V wakes behind

b1.n: Hammer Tail Swing: tails swing out one after another, splashes bursting

b2.n: Dark Swimmer Scales: wet dark scales glint in a row, sheen flecks

b3.n: Swimming Dodge Trick: monitors scull out in all directions and slip back, bubbles left behind

spice-monitor.notes: A cinnamon-red island monitor with clove-dark spots and a saffron throat; it smells of spice and leaves a trail of spice dust that stings.

u0.n: Spice Bite: the spice monitor lunges off the edge, a fall of cinnamon dust stinging after it

u1.n: Tail Whip: cinnamon-banded tails uncoil and crack off the edge

u2.n: Fork Tongue: snouts blink up at spots and flick forked tongues to taste the air

u3.n: Cinnamon Cloud: star-anise pods burst out of the edge in a cloud of spice powder and drift back

b0.n: Cinnamon Jaw: a spice monitor shoves out jaw-first and drops back in a puff of spice

b1.n: Sweeping Tail: one long tail sweeps the length of the edge

p.b2: Crusted Scales: curled cinnamon-bark quills line the edge like a crusted hide, turning

b3.n: Tasting Flick: tongues flick in and out, spice powder falling off them

komodo-pup.notes: A gangly young komodo of island beaches: sand-spotted, big-headed, with a long yellow forked tongue it never stops flicking; it trips, hides in sand and drools.

u0.n: Pup Tail Trip: pups sprawl at spots, their tails hooked together into an ankle-high tripline

u1.n: Sand Flop: the pups flop belly-down and scoot out in a spray of sand, then scamper back

u2.n: Dune Hide: sand mounds line the edge, a pup's eye peeping out of each and blinking

u3.n: Low Watch: pups lie low along the edge, only their forked tongues flicking to watch

p.b0: Trip Bite: komodo pups launch off the edge tongue-first and snap

b1.n: Ankle Sweep: one pup scampers the length of the edge at ankle height

b2.n: Crouched Scales: spotted scales bristle up along the edge as the pup crouches

b3.n: Sly Drool Trap: sticky drool strings hang at spots, tied in a trap

smooth-snake.notes: A pale grey, glossy, round-pupilled grassland snake that lives under warm stones, suns itself on them and squeezes its prey in its coils.

u0.n: Coil Squeeze: grey coils grip at spots and tighten, bound together by a glossy line

u1.n: Scale Slip: glossy smooth scales slip out of reach and back, a sheen running over them

u2.n: Hiss Feint: coils rear up at one spot then another, hissing, never striking

p.u3: Stone Sunning: a flat warm stone with the snake draped on it rises, heat shimmering off it

b0.n: Warmstone Fang: small fangs launch off the edge, a bead at each tip

b1.n: Coil-Snap Whip: a coil springs out of the edge and snaps back tight

p.b2: Sun-Warmed Scales: warm stones line the edge, the smooth snake basking along them

b3.n: Sleek Venom Feint: fangs flash at spots and vanish

water-snake.notes: An olive water snake with dark crossbands and a flat head, swimming the shallows of wetland and coast in an S, hunting fish among the reeds.

u0.n: Water Snap: a banded snake shoots along the waterline head-first, bubbles in its wake

u1.n: Tight Coil: banded snakes lie in tight S folds along the edge, bands breathing

u2.n: Bank Slide: the snake slides off a mud bank out of the edge and slaps back, mud splats

p.u3: Reed Weave: reed stems stand along the edge, the banded snake weaving in and out of them

b0.n: Shallows Fang: banded swimmers launch off the edge, bubbles behind

b1.n: Fishing Lash: silver fish flipped up out of the shallows end over end

b2.n: Olive Banded Shield: reeds stand in a row with the banded snake woven through them

b3.n: Reed Bait Trick: a reed twitches at one spot, then another, the snake waiting behind

tree-snake.notes: A slim, long, bright-green rainforest snake that drapes from boughs like a vine and hides among leaves until one of the leaves strikes.

u0.n: Branch Drape: green snakes drape off the boughs out of reach and coil back up

u1.n: Leaf Strike: a spray of leaves flies off the edge and one of them bites, red tongue flicking

u2.n: Bough Cover: leaves line the edge, rustling; now and then one leaf has an eye

u3.n: Coil Drop: the snake lets go of its bough, drops out of the edge and springs back

p.b0: Branch-Drop Strike: draped snakes drop off their boughs and fly out

b1.n: Vine-Coil Lash: snakes hang at spots, coiled together like vines

b2.n: Hanging Green Shield: leaves hang along the edge, dew running down them

b3.n: Unseen Venom Jet: a hidden snout spits a fan of venom that falls

night-adder.notes: A dark, thick night adder of grassland and desert with a zigzag down its back and red eyes; it lies on warm roads at night and strikes from an S-coil.

u0.n: Fang Strike: an adder strikes the full length of the edge from its S-coil

u1.n: Quick Fangs: pairs of fangs launch off the edge one after another, venom beads flying

p.u2: Night Coil: dark coils lie along the edge, two red eyes glowing and blinking in each

u3.n: Road Sit: a strip of warm night road pushes out of the edge with an adder on it, heat rising

p.b0: Zigzag Fang: zigzag adders launch off the edge

b1.n: Roadside Coil Lash: an adder coil shoves out and snaps back

b2.n: Zigzag Back Scales: adders lie along the edge, the dark zigzag down their backs

b3.n: Warm Road Lure: warm road patches shimmer at spots, luring

dust-sidewinder.notes: A small pale desert sidewinder that moves sideways in loops, leaving J-shaped tracks in the sand, with little horns over its eyes for burying itself.

u0.n: Side Wind: sidewinders loop sideways out of the edge and back, J-tracks pressed in the sand

u1.n: Dust Fang: fangs drop venom beads into the sand, dust puffing

u2.n: Sand Skim: one sidewinder skims the length of the edge sideways, sand dust behind

u3.n: Sideways Skirt: the horned head pops out of the sand at one spot, then another

b0.n: Sideways Fang: fangs launch off the edge

b1.n: Sand Tail Slap: a sidewinder loop slaps out of the edge and back

p.b2: Sidestep Scales: horned heads peep out of the sand along the edge

b3.n: Dust Sprinkle: sidewinders slip off the edge in a sprinkle of dust

dune-racer.notes: A thin, pale, striped desert-and-coast racer, the fastest snake on the dunes: a straight streak, a spit of venom, gone into the heat mirage.

u0.n: Racer Spit: snouts spit fans of venom off the edge

u1.n: Fang Flick: fangs flick at one spot, then another, too fast to follow

p.u2: Mirage Flit: heat-mirage lines wobble out of the edge with a ghost racer in them, then flicker back

u3.n: Sting Dash: one striped racer streaks the full length of the edge

p.b0: Dash Fang: racers dart off the edge in straight streaks

b1.n: Twin Sting Lash: twin fangs shove out of the edge and snap back

b2.n: Pale Streak Scales: pale scales shingle along the edge, a gold glint

b3.n: Burst Spit: spitting snouts burst out in all directions
